{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-in-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"89a890f3c77dc7b933e879f208ba6039f49e9c41bd60fec3baa2eb1f9247aa76","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","source_liveness_sha256":"4d2b75b9a10fb774f53fb2d906a3a7a7f75f5e9387f8b4ddcd423e9b7828d59b"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Document, teen and service confusables and continuation","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: identity versus lawful status, residency date windows, affidavit signers, and continuation facts on accepted documents, translations, teen tips, parent tips and services","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: identity versus lawful status, residency date windows, affidavit signers, and continuation facts on accepted documents, translations, teen tips, parent tips and services
Confusable pairs from the appendices on documents, teen driving and BMV services, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
A delayed birth certificate for someone born abroad works for identity, while lawful status must be shown another way. [A01]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable identity versus lawful status.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A03
A W-2, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year, whereas an insurance policy must be dated within one year of the application. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency; confusable date windows.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A03
For an incapacitated applicant the affidavit is signed by a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least 18, while for a homeless applicant it is signed by a representative of the agency or nonprofit that serves them. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency affidavit; confusable signers.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified. [A01]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth. [A01]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions. [A01]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A02
A Notice of Action form proves lawful status only if the BMV verifies that DHS received it without denying action and the applicant also submits pertaining federal-agency documents showing lawful status [A02].
Why it matters: group lawful status; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A02
Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document. [A02]
Why it matters: group lawful status; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can prove residency. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
An applicant living in a motor vehicle such as a motor home needs another Indiana resident to sign the affidavit at a branch and must show Indiana income tax payment plus current title and registration records with the BMV. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency affidavit; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A04
A translator's statement must attest that the translation is accurate and that the translator is competent. [A04]
Why it matters: group translations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A04
Illegal or unsafe speed is a common factor in single-vehicle crashes, while driver inattention is a common factor in multiple-vehicle crashes. [A04]
Why it matters: group teen risks; confusable single versus multiple vehicle crashes.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A04
Teens are advised to adjust seats and mirrors before each drive, wait until stopped to adjust the radio, and avoid loud music that could hide a siren or horn. [A04]
Why it matters: group teen tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A04
Even with a green light, be ready to stop as you approach an intersection in case the light changes. [A04]
Why it matters: group teen tips; link to signals chapter.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A04
A seat belt is required by law and is the most effective way to lower the risk of being hurt or killed in a crash. [A04]
Why it matters: group teen risks; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A05
Parents are urged to set a good example, require seat belts, choose vehicles for safety rather than image, and grant progressive privileges as the teen shows good judgment. [A05]
Why it matters: group parent tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A05
The manual calls driver education a first step and says parents play a crucial role in teaching teens to drive. [A05]
Why it matters: group parent tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A05
Failing to register with the Selective Service can bring up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, and registration applies to US citizens. [A05]
Why it matters: group services; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A05
BMV forms are available on IN.gov/BMV or at any branch, and mail-in voter registration forms exist for people not at a branch. [A05]
Why it matters: group services; dynamic service detail.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A06
Checks for registration renewal should be made out to BMV or Bureau of Motor Vehicles. [A06]
Why it matters: group services; dynamic service detail.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0078]
